Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specific asks so they can finish a commercial summary for leadership: 

1) Can Redwood amortize the annual platform fee across a 6-month pilot + 18-month production term (effectively 24 months) to reduce the upfront hit for our finance team? They prefer even amortization but are open to a small front-loaded schedule.

2) We need clarity on the SRE/Oncall retainer vs per-incident support — which would you recommend for a healthcare deployment handling PHI? They are sensitive to response-time SLAs and want predictable ops costs.

3) Exit protections: if we terminate early or choose a different stack after year 1, what rights do we have for data export and a code/keys escrow? Procurement wants the minimum friction for moving workloads.

Attached is a high-level SOW outline NovaClinic put together. Can you please respond with one-page options we can show finance? We're aiming to finalize commercial terms by June 6.

Thanks — Rachael

--

Hi Rachael — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers below; I'll follow with a one-pager and the amortization workbook.

1) Amortization: we can offer to spread the platform fee over 24 months (6m pilot + 18m production) with a small 10% onboarding/front-load in month 1 to cover provisioning and security attestation work. That keeps monthly finance impact low while covering implementation risk.

2) Support: for PHI workloads we recommend the SRE retainer (guaranteed response windows, on-call rotation, runbook handoffs) for predictable costs and faster MTTR. Per-incident can be cheaper if incidents are rare, but it's variable and procurement doesn't like P&L unpredictability. 

3) Exit: standard data export within 30 days included. For escrow, we can offer a limited code/keys escrow via a neutral custodian for an additional one-time fee (or rolled into the amortization). We'll propose a clause that includes assistance for safe handover and an option for 90-day transitional SRE support at a discounted rate.

I'll attach: 1) amortization spreadsheet (breakout by month), 2) two commercial packaging options (A: Retainer + amortized fee, B: Lower platform fee + per-incident top-up). Expect docs in next email.

—Mateo

Mateo — looping in pricing to make sure we align. Notes for the one-pager:

- Option A (Recommended): 24-month amortization, 10% onboarding upfront, monthly amortized line item. SRE retainer tier 2 (24/7 coverage with 2hr P1 response) priced as monthly retainer. Include one-time escrow setup fee ($25k) or roll into amortization.

- Option B (Lower fixed platform fee): Reduce platform fee by 20% but remove amortization; offer per-incident credits and a 6-month discounted retainer for first year. Better if NovaClinic has internal ops capacity.

- Add explicit export SLA (30 days) + one week of export verification by Redwood. Escrow terms: access only on insolvency/contract breach, custodian-managed, redaction of proprietary components allowed.

Jordan — can you draft the short SOW language for export/escrow and the retainer tiers? I can finalize pricing lines for the workbook.

Thanks — Irene
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference

Hi Rachael — attaching the short SOW excerpt below and a clean one-pager (see Drive link). High-level SOW excerpt: 

--- SOW excerpt (for inclusion in term sheet) ---
1) Data export and verification: Redwood will provide a full export of customer data in common formats (JSON, CSV) within 30 calendar days of contract termination request. Redwood will perform a verification pass and provide an export checklist.
2) Escrow: Redwood will deposit a minimal set of artifacts with a neutral custodian. Artifacts are released only upon agreed triggers (insolvency, sustained breach) and are redacted to protect proprietary model weights and internal tooling.
3) Transitional support: Upon termination, Redwood will provide up to 90 days of transitional SRE support at a reduced daily rate to help lift-and-shift.

--- end excerpt ---
